caseMeta.title: Acute Decompensated Heart Failure - Hospital Day 3
learningObjectives: Recognize signs of fluid overload and respond to diuresis (I&O, weights, K/Mg, orthostatic BP).
Teach heart failure self-care: daily weights, sodium and fluid limits, and symptom zones.
Interpret BNP, creatinine, potassium and magnesium trends with diuresis.
Connect assessment findings, labs and orders to prioritize nursing care.
Safely administer medications using the MAR and linked monitoring data.

orders.name: Cardiac (2 g sodium) diet; fluid restriction 1,500 mL/day
orders.instructions: Restrict sodium to 2 g/day and fluids to 1,500 mL/day.

orders.name: Bed rest with bathroom privileges
orders.instructions: Conserve energy; HOB elevated.

orders.name: Up with assistance; ambulate in hall three times daily
orders.instructions: Monitor SpO2 and symptoms with activity.

orders.name: Oxygen via nasal cannula
orders.instructions: Titrate to SpO2 92% or higher; wean as diuresis improves.

orders.name: Strict intake and output
orders.instructions: Record all intake and output; document urine after each diuretic dose.

orders.name: Daily weight
orders.instructions: Same scale each morning, after voiding, before breakfast; record in kg.

orders.name: Continuous cardiac monitoring (telemetry)
orders.instructions: Notify provider for new arrhythmia, HR above 130 or below 50.

orders.name: Head of bed elevated 30-45 degrees
orders.instructions: Elevate for orthopnea; monitor for dyspnea.

orders.name: BMP and magnesium daily (potassium and magnesium goals 4.0 and 2.0)
orders.instructions: Replace per protocol with diuresis.

orders.name: Respiratory therapy evaluate and treat
orders.instructions: Assess work of breathing and oxygen need; wean as able.

orders.name: Heart failure education
orders.instructions: Daily weights, 2 g sodium, fluid limit, medication adherence, symptoms to report; teach-back before discharge.

orders.name: Fluid restriction 1,000 mL/day
orders.instructions: Limit total oral fluids to 1,000 mL per 24 hours (including IV fluids and medications).
nursingConsiderations: Track all oral and IV intake carefully.

orders.name: No BP, blood draws or IV access in left arm (AV fistula)
orders.instructions: Protect the fistula arm. Check thrill and bruit every shift.

orders.name: Renal dosing review / avoid nephrotoxins
orders.instructions: Pharmacy to dose all medications for ESRD. Avoid NSAIDs, morphine, and enoxaparin.

orders.name: Supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula
orders.instructions: Start 1-2 L/min; titrate to SpO2 88-92%. Do not exceed target (CO2 retention risk).
nursingConsiderations: Goal SpO2 is 88-92%, NOT higher; notify provider for drowsiness or SpO2 below 88%.

orders.name: Delirium precautions and frequent reorientation
orders.instructions: Lights on by day, off at night; glasses/hearing aids; reorient often; avoid restraints; limit sedatives and anticholinergics.

orders.name: Fall precautions (bed alarm on)
orders.instructions: Bed alarm on, low bed, frequent rounding, toileting schedule.

orders.name: Tobacco cessation counseling
orders.instructions: Offer cessation counseling and quitline information before discharge.

orders.name: CIWA-Ar alcohol withdrawal assessment
orders.frequency: Every 4 hours (every 1 hour after PRN dose)
orders.instructions: Score CIWA-Ar; give lorazepam per protocol for score of 10 or greater. Notify provider for score above 20, seizure, or hallucinations.
nursingConsiderations: Seizure and fall precautions; keep room quiet and well lit.

orders.name: Vital signs
orders.instructions: Notify provider for SBP below 90 or above 180, HR above 120 or below 50, RR above 28, SpO2 below 90%, or temperature above 101.5 F.

orders.name: CBC and basic metabolic panel
orders.instructions: Draw at 0500.

orders.name: Chest x-ray, portable
orders.instructions: Perform Chest x-ray, portable.

orders.name: 12-lead ECG
orders.instructions: Perform 12-lead ECG.

orders.name: Transthoracic echocardiogram
orders.instructions: Perform Transthoracic echocardiogram.

orders.name: Consult: Cardiology
orders.instructions: Acute decompensated HFrEF

orders.name: Consult: Nephrology
orders.instructions: Volume overload in ESRD patient

orders.name: sevelamer carbonate (RENVELA) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 800 mg Oral TID.

medication.importantInfo: Give WITH meals. Hold if patient is NPO or not eating.

orders.name: B-complex with vitamin C and folic acid (NEPHRO-VITE) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 1 tablet Oral Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Give after dialysis on dialysis days.

orders.name: amlodipine (NORVASC) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 10 mg Oral Daily. Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.
nursingConsiderations: Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.

medication.importantInfo: Check BP before giving. Monitor for peripheral edema.

orders.name: carvedilol (COREG) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 6.25 mg Oral BID. Hold and notify provider if HR below 55 or SBP below 100.
nursingConsiderations: Hold and notify provider if HR below 55 or SBP below 100.

medication.importantInfo: Give with food. Check BP and HR before giving.

orders.name: apixaban (ELIQUIS) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 5 mg Oral BID.

medication.importantInfo: Monitor for bleeding. HIGH-ALERT: do not give if the patient is scheduled for or just had surgery until the surgeon clears it.

orders.name: fluticasone-salmeterol (ADVAIR DISKUS) inhaler
orders.instructions: Administer 250/50 mcg, 1 inhalation Inhaled BID.

medication.importantInfo: Rinse mouth after use. Check inhaler technique.

orders.name: nicotine (NICODERM CQ) 24 hour patch
orders.instructions: Administer 21 mg Transdermal Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Rotate sites; remove old patch. Do not smoke while wearing patch.

orders.name: thiamine tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 100 mg Oral Daily.

orders.name: folic acid tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 1 mg Oral Daily.

orders.name: multivitamin tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 1 tablet Oral Daily.

orders.name: ipratropium-albuterol (DUONEB) nebulizer solution
orders.instructions: Administer 3 mL Nebulized Every 6 hours.

medication.importantInfo: Given by RT. Assess breath sounds, HR and work of breathing before and after.

orders.name: donepezil (ARICEPT) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 10 mg Oral Nightly at bedtime.

medication.importantInfo: May cause bradycardia, nausea, vivid dreams. Check HR before giving.

orders.name: acetaminophen (TYLENOL) tablet
orders.frequency: Every 6 hours PRN mild pain (avoid NSAIDs)
orders.instructions: Administer 650 mg Oral Every 6 hours PRN mild pain (avoid NSAIDs).

medication.importantInfo: Avoid NSAIDs in heart failure (fluid retention).

orders.name: nitroglycerin (NITROSTAT) sublingual tablet
orders.frequency: Every 5 minutes up to 3 doses PRN chest pain
orders.instructions: Administer 0.4 mg Sublingual Every 5 minutes up to 3 doses PRN chest pain. Hold for SBP below 100.

medication.importantInfo: Check BP before each dose; hold for SBP below 100. Call provider for chest pain.

orders.name: albuterol (PROVENTIL) nebulizer solution
orders.frequency: Every 2 hours PRN wheezing or shortness of breath
orders.instructions: Administer 2.5 mg Nebulized Every 2 hours PRN wheezing or shortness of breath.

medication.importantInfo: Check HR before and after; may cause tremor and tachycardia.

orders.name: lorazepam (ATIVAN) tablet
orders.frequency: Every 4 hours PRN CIWA-Ar 10 or greater
orders.instructions: Administer 1-2 mg per CIWA score Oral Every 4 hours PRN CIWA-Ar 10 or greater.

medication.importantInfo: Hold for sedation (RASS -2 or lower) or RR below 12. Reassess CIWA 1 hour after dose.

notes.title: Hemodialysis Treatment Note
notes.author: Dialysis RN (Inpatient Dialysis Unit)
notes.summary: Hemodialysis completed; 2013 mL removed.
notes.body:
**Treatment**
- Hemodialysis 0800-1130 (3.5 hours) via left upper arm AV fistula; two 15-gauge needles, good flows.
- Pre: BP 163/88, HR 95; weight above dry weight.
- Ultrafiltration goal and removed: 2013 mL. Heparin per protocol.
- Tolerated well without cramping or hypotension; needles removed, hemostasis achieved in 10 minutes, fistula thrill present.

**Post-treatment**
- Post-dialysis weight recorded. Give renal vitamin and hold antihypertensives if SBP below 100.

notes.title: Hospitalist Progress Note
notes.author: S. Patel, MD
notes.summary: Hospital day 3: Near dry weight; transitioning to oral diuretic.
notes.body:
**Hospital Day 3**

**Interval events / subjective**
Feels much better. Walking in hall without dyspnea; sleeping flat. Appetite good.
- Hemodialysis (3.5 h) (09/02/26 0800): completed

**Objective**
- Vitals (24 h): Tmax 98.4 F; HR 95-100; BP 158-168/88-92; RR 19-21; SpO2 90-92%; pain 0/10
- Current: T 98.2 F, HR 95, BP 163/88, RR 20, SpO2 92% on 2 l nasal cannula, pain 0/10
- I&O (24 h): in 1246 mL / out 332 mL
- Diet: Fluid restriction 1,000 mL/day; Activity: Up with assistance; ambulate in hall three times daily

**Exam**
- General: Awake and alert, in no acute distress.
- Cardiovascular: Atrial fibrillation, rate controlled; S1 S2 with S3 gallop; 2/6 systolic murmur at apex. Edema: 1+ pedal edema.
- Respiratory: Faint bibasilar crackles; unlabored.
- Abdomen: Soft, mildly distended, mild hepatic tenderness. Bowel sounds: active in all four quadrants.
- Neurologic: Oriented to person only (baseline per family).
- Skin: Cool extremities, mild peripheral cyanosis, dry.

**Labs**
- BNP 1236 (H); Sodium 135 (L) (stable from 133); Potassium 5.0 (up from 4.5); Magnesium 2.0 (up from 1.8); BUN 56 (H) (down from 60); Creatinine 6.08 (H) (stable from 6.24); Glucose 96 (stable from 99)

**Medications**
- Scheduled: sevelamer carbonate 800 mg Oral; B-complex with vitamin C and folic acid 1 tablet Oral; amlodipine 10 mg Oral; carvedilol 6.25 mg Oral; apixaban 5 mg Oral; ipratropium-albuterol nebulizer solution 3 mL Nebulized; fluticasone-salmeterol inhaler 250/50 mcg, 1 inhalation Inhaled; donepezil 10 mg Oral; nicotine 24 hour patch 21 mg Transdermal; thiamine 100 mg Oral
- PRN: acetaminophen; nitroglycerin sublingual; albuterol; lorazepam

**Assessment and plan**
74-year-old female, hospital day 3.

**Acute decompensated heart failure**
- Near euvolemia; transitioning to an oral regimen; renal function stable.
- Switch to oral furosemide 40 mg BID; observe 24 hours for weight stability.
- Room air; continue carvedilol; optimize GDMT per cardiology.
- Heart failure teaching with teach-back; scale and BP cuff at home.

**End-stage renal disease on hemodialysis**
- Hemodialysis per nephrology (Mon/Wed/Fri); no further volume removal today unless symptomatic.
- Renal diet, 1 L fluid restriction, sevelamer with meals when eating.
- Renally dose all medications; avoid NSAIDs, morphine, enoxaparin.
- Protect left arm fistula.

**Hypertension**
- Continue home antihypertensive; BP goal below 140/90.

**Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction**
- Euvolemic to mildly dry on exam; continue beta blocker; judicious IV fluids with daily weights.
- Continue home diuretic.

**Atrial fibrillation**
- Rate controlled on metoprolol/carvedilol.
- Continue apixaban; monitor for bleeding.

**Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease**
- Scheduled DuoNebs q6h with PRN albuterol; maintenance inhaler continued.
- Oxygen goal SpO2 88-92%; avoid over-oxygenation.
- Tobacco cessation counseling and nicotine replacement.

**Dementia**
- Delirium precautions; avoid benzodiazepines/anticholinergics; family at bedside if possible.
- Capacity limited; involve surrogate decision maker.

**Disposition**
- Discharge home in 1-2 days on oral diuretic.
- Code status: Full Code.

notes.title: Respiratory Therapy Note
notes.author: D. Moore, RRT
notes.summary: RT assessment: 2 L nasal cannula, SpO2 92%.
notes.body:
**Assessment**
- O2 therapy: 2 L nasal cannula; SpO2 92%; RR 20.
- Breath sounds: Faint bibasilar crackles. Work of breathing: unlabored.
- Cough: Dry, worse lying flat.


**Treatments**
- Scheduled nebulizer: ipratropium-albuterol nebulizer solution 3 mL Every 6 hours; tolerated, no adverse effects.

**Plan**
- Titrate O2 to SpO2 88-92%; continue nebulizers; reinforce inhaler technique and pursed-lip breathing.

notes.title: Nursing Progress Note
notes.author: L. Bennett, RN
notes.summary: Night shift summary: Near dry weight; transitioning to oral diuretic.
notes.body:
**Shift summary (night shift, hospital day 3)**
- Neuro: Oriented to person only (baseline per family). Pain: 0/10.
- Cardiac: Atrial fibrillation, rate controlled; edema: 1+ pedal edema. Vitals this shift: Tmax 98.3 F; HR 95-99; BP 158-163/88-92; RR 19-21; SpO2 90-92%; pain 0/10.
- Respiratory: Faint bibasilar crackles; 2 l nasal cannula, SpO2 92%.
- GI: Soft, mildly distended, mild hepatic tenderness; diet Fluid restriction 1,000 mL/day; nausea/vomiting: none.
- GU: Minimal urine output (oliguric ESRD). I&O this shift: in 854 mL, out 217 mL.
- Skin / lines: Cool extremities, mild peripheral cyanosis, dry. Peripheral IV (Right forearm): patent; Nasal cannula (oxygen) (Nares): in place; AV fistula (Left upper arm): patent.
- Mobility / safety: Up with assistance; ambulate in hall three times daily; High risk: bed alarm on, bed low, hourly rounding.

**Events and interventions**
- Room air saturation 95%; trace pedal edema; ambulating independently.
- Teach-back on daily weights and 2 g sodium diet.

**Education**
- When to call the doctor: weight gain over 2-3 lb in a day or 5 lb in a week, worsening swelling or shortness of breath.

**Plan / handoff**
- Activity: up with assistance; ambulate in hall three times daily. Discharge home in 1-2 days on oral diuretic.
- Call light within reach; bed alarm per fall risk.

- Respiratory: Crackles to the lower third bilaterally; 2 l nasal cannula, SpO2 90%.

- Skin / lines: Cool extremities, mild peripheral cyanosis, dry. Peripheral IV (Right forearm): patent; Nasal cannula (oxygen) (Nares): in place; AV fistula (Left upper arm): patent.

notes.title: Occupational Therapy Initial Evaluation
notes.author: C. Rivera, OTR/L
notes.summary: OT evaluation: ADL and cognitive screen.
notes.body:
**Prior level of function**
- Lives alone; needs assistance with some ADLs, uses walker.

**Current status**
- Grooming and upper-body dressing: set-up / supervision. Lower-body dressing and toileting: minimal assist.
- Cognition: Oriented to person only (baseline per family).

**Plan**
- OT 3-5x/week; energy conservation and ADL retraining; reassess equipment needs.

notes.title: Physical Therapy Initial Evaluation
notes.author: A. Kim, PT, DPT
notes.summary: PT evaluation: minimal assist; 75 feet with rolling walker.
notes.body:
**Prior level of function**
- Lives alone; uses walker for mobility.

**Current status**
- Bed mobility and transfers: minimal assist.
- Gait: 75 feet with rolling walker; steady with no loss of balance.
- Vitals with activity: T 98.3 F, HR 100, BP 162/92, RR 20, SpO2 90% on 2 l nasal cannula, pain 0/10; tolerated well.
- Pain: 0/10 with movement.

**Assessment**
- Decreased mobility and endurance related to acute illness; good rehab potential.

**Plan / recommendation**
- PT daily while inpatient; progress gait and stairs.
- Discharge recommendation: Home with home health PT and 24-hour supervision, or short-term rehab if goals not met.

notes.title: Case Management Initial Assessment
notes.author: P. Lawson, RN, CCM
notes.summary: Anticipated discharge: Return to assisted living with therapy.
notes.body:
**Social situation**
- Lives alone. Insurance: Medicare with supplemental plan. Transportation: family/self.
- Prior function: walker.

**Barriers**
- lives alone with limited help at home
- uses walker at baseline
- cognitive impairment; needs 24-hour supervision
- current tobacco use (cessation resources offered)
- heavy alcohol use (outpatient treatment resources offered)

**Anticipated discharge plan**
- Return to assisted living with therapy.
- Estimated discharge: within the next 1-3 days.

**Plan**
- Follow daily for medical readiness, therapy recommendations and equipment/home health needs.

notes.title: Registered Dietitian Nutrition Assessment
notes.author: N. Foster, RD, LDN
notes.summary: Nutrition assessment: Fluid restriction 1,000 mL/day.
notes.body:
**Assessment**
- Ht 163 cm, Wt 70 kg, BMI 26.3.
- Current diet: Fluid restriction 1,000 mL/day. Intake: fair, about 50-75% of meals.
- Pertinent labs: Sodium 133 (L) (stable from 131); Potassium 4.5 (stable from 4.6); Glucose 99 (down from 107); Creatinine 6.24 (H) (stable from 6.10); Phosphorus 5.4 (H).

**Estimated needs**
- Energy 1750-2100 kcal/day; protein 84-91 g/day; fluid 1,000 mL/day.

**Recommendations**
- Continue Fluid restriction 1,000 mL/day; encourage protein at each meal; oral supplement if intake stays below 50%.
- Renal diet teaching (sodium, potassium, phosphorus); 2 g sodium teaching; follow up in 3-4 days.

notes.title: Transthoracic echocardiogram
notes.author: H. Banerjee, MD
notes.summary: LVEF 30-35% with global hypokinesis, mild-to-moderate mitral regurgitation, elevated filling pressures.
notes.body:
**Indication**
- Evaluate LV function and valves

**Findings**
Dilated left ventricle with global hypokinesis. LVEF 30-35%. Moderate left atrial enlargement. Mild-to-moderate functional mitral regurgitation. RVSP 45 mmHg. Small pericardial effusion without tamponade. IVC dilated with reduced collapse.

**Impression**
- LVEF 30-35% with global hypokinesis, mild-to-moderate mitral regurgitation, elevated filling pressures.

notes.title: Hospitalist History and Physical
notes.author: S. Patel, MD
notes.summary: Admission H&P for acute decompensated heart failure.
notes.body:
**Chief complaint**
- Shortness of breath, orthopnea and leg swelling

**History of present illness**
74-year-old female with chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF about 35%) presenting with 4 days of progressive shortness of breath, orthopnea (now needs 3 pillows), paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, bilateral leg swelling and an 8-pound weight gain. Admits to eating salty foods at a recent family gathering and missing several doses of furosemide. No chest pain, palpitations, fever or syncope.

**Past medical history**
- End-stage renal disease on hemodialysis (Mon/Wed/Fri, left arm AV fistula); Hypertension; Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF about 35%); Atrial fibrillation (CHA2DS2-VASc elevated, on apixaban); COPD; Dementia

**Past surgical history**
- Hysterectomy; Bowel resection / colectomy

**Home medications**
- sevelamer carbonate (RENVELA) 800 mg Oral TID
- B-complex with vitamin C and folic acid (NEPHRO-VITE) 1 tablet Oral Daily
- lisinopril (PRINIVIL,ZESTRIL) 20 mg Oral Daily
- carvedilol (COREG) 6.25 mg Oral BID
- apixaban (ELIQUIS) 5 mg Oral BID
- ipratropium-albuterol (DUONEB) nebulizer solution 3 mL Nebulized Every 6 hours
- albuterol (PROVENTIL) nebulizer solution 2.5 mg Nebulized Every 4 hours
- fluticasone-salmeterol (ADVAIR DISKUS) inhaler 250/50 mcg, 1 inhalation Inhaled BID
- donepezil (ARICEPT) 10 mg Oral Nightly at bedtime
- (Home tiotropium replaced by scheduled DuoNebs (avoid duplicate anticholinergic).)

**Allergies**
- Penicillin (Hives)

**Family history**
- Mother with hypertension; father with coronary artery disease. No known family history of bowel disease or cancer.

**Social history**
- Lives alone; uses walker at baseline; tobacco: current ≥1 ppd; alcohol: heavy daily; other substances: none.

**Review of systems**
- Positive for dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, PND, leg swelling and weight gain. Negative for chest pain, palpitations, syncope, fever, cough with sputum and abdominal pain.

**Vitals**
- T 98.3 F, HR 108, BP 176/102, RR 23, SpO2 90% on 3 l nasal cannula, pain 1/10 | Wt 70 kg, BMI 26.3

**Physical exam**
- General: Awake and alert, in no acute distress.
- Cardiovascular: Atrial fibrillation, rate controlled; S1 S2 with S3 gallop; 2/6 systolic murmur at apex. Edema: 2+ pitting bilateral lower extremity edema to the knees.
- Respiratory: Bibasilar crackles to mid-lung fields; tachypneic, speaks in short sentences, prefers upright position.
- Abdomen: Soft, mildly distended, mild hepatic tenderness. Bowel sounds: active in all four quadrants.
- Neurologic: Oriented to person only (baseline per family).
- Skin: Cool extremities, mild peripheral cyanosis, dry.

**Data**
- Labs: BNP 1236 (H); Troponin I 0.03 (stable from 0.03); Sodium 131 (L); Potassium 4.6; BUN 58 (H); Creatinine 6.10 (H); Glucose 107; Magnesium 1.7
- Chest x-ray, portable: Cardiomegaly with pulmonary edema and small bilateral pleural effusions.
- 12-lead ECG: Atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response, rate 92. Left ventricular hypertrophy. Old left bundle branch block, unchanged.

**Assessment and plan**
74-year-old female with a history of end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, hypertension, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, dementia admitted with acute decompensated heart failure.

**Acute decompensated heart failure**
- Volume overload from dietary sodium excess and missed diuretic; troponin negative; BNP 1,240.
- Urgent hemodialysis with ultrafiltration (ESRD); no loop diuretic.
- Oxygen to keep SpO2 92% or higher; telemetry.
- Replace potassium (goal 4.0) and magnesium (goal 2.0).
- 2 g sodium diet and 1.5 L fluid restriction.
- Echocardiogram and cardiology consult; hold ACE inhibitor if creatinine rises.

**End-stage renal disease on hemodialysis**
- Hemodialysis per nephrology (Mon/Wed/Fri); no further volume removal today unless symptomatic.
- Renal diet, 1 L fluid restriction, sevelamer with meals when eating.
- Renally dose all medications; avoid NSAIDs, morphine, enoxaparin.
- Protect left arm fistula.

**Hypertension**
- Continue home antihypertensive; BP goal below 140/90.

**Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction**
- Euvolemic to mildly dry on exam; continue beta blocker; judicious IV fluids with daily weights.
- Continue home diuretic.

**Atrial fibrillation**
- Rate controlled on metoprolol/carvedilol.
- Continue apixaban; monitor for bleeding.

**Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease**
- Scheduled DuoNebs q6h with PRN albuterol; maintenance inhaler continued.
- Oxygen goal SpO2 88-92%; avoid over-oxygenation.
- Tobacco cessation counseling and nicotine replacement.

**Dementia**
- Delirium precautions; avoid benzodiazepines/anticholinergics; family at bedside if possible.
- Capacity limited; involve surrogate decision maker.

**Prophylaxis / code status**
- DVT prophylaxis per orders; fall precautions.
- Code status: Full Code.
